articles.title: June 15, 2026 — System Architecture Notes (Raw Annotations)
articles.summary: Raw annotations on kernel behavior, SKE protocol characteristics, cognitive load, and early architectural hypotheses.
articles.contentHtml:
Observation: Kernel Behavior & Conceptual Stability

  • Kernel structure tends to converge toward a deterministic state machine.
  • Attempts to add flexibility introduce noise, so system coherence decreases.
  • Removing unnecessary layers increases clarity and reduces cognitive load.
  • Kernel appears to require a strict separation between logic and execution.
  • Early signs suggest invariants can serve as the primary stabilizing mechanism.

Observation: SKE Protocol Characteristics

  • SKE naturally forms a 3-boundary model: cognitive → scheduling → execution.
  • Message types (JobSpec, EngineRequest, EngineResult) remain stable across iterations.
  • Security invariants appear to be the correct abstraction for trust boundaries.
  • Protocol complexity remains low if semantics stay inside the kernel.

Measurement: Cognitive Load During Design

  • High load when mixing conceptual layers (kernel + scheduler).
  • Lower load when isolating each layer and evaluating independently.
  • Visual diagrams reduce ambiguity by roughly 40–60 percent (subjective estimate).
  • Fractal/geometric visual identity improves focus unexpectedly but consistently.

Hypotheses

  1. Kernel must remain the single source of cognitive semantics.
  2. Scheduler must remain purely operational, with no reasoning.
  3. Engines must remain stateless and replaceable.
  4. Security invariants must be first-class, not post-hoc.
  5. Agentic general architecture is viable only if invariants are stable.

Evaluation: Current Architecture State

  • Kernel concept: stable enough for first formalization.
  • SKE: requires compression into a minimal formal spec.
  • Invariants: partially defined and need consolidation.
  • Agentic layer: conceptual shape emerging, not ready for formalization.
  • Visual identity: consistent direction; supports cognitive workflow.

Insight

  • System coherence increases when each layer has one responsibility.
  • Invariants act as anchors for reasoning and design decisions.
  • Architecture behaves like a constraint-driven system, not a feature-driven one.
  • Early formalization reduces future refactoring cost significantly.

Next Steps

  • Refine kernel invariants and consolidate them into a minimal stable set.
  • Draft a minimal kernel spec focused on state, transitions, and invariants.
  • Compress SKE into a one-page formal spec and remove redundancy.
  • Define failure modes and identify weak points in the architecture.
  • Map agentic layers and outline responsibilities without implementation.
  • Reassess trust boundaries and verify alignment with invariants.

Closing Thought

This entry captures the first measurable movements of the system: kernel stabilization, protocol simplification, and invariant emergence. The IDL will serve as the running log for tracking these shifts, validating hypotheses, and documenting the evolution of the architecture over time.
